findings.message: HR still has two 'today's. addPerson, recordLeaver and the status job now use the entity's own today (entityToday). But changePersonRun's default effective date (line 53), its 'person fields change today' check (line 58), and contracts.ts getPerson/listPeople/getEmployment (lines 74, 90, 109) still use UTC today(). In the hours when the entity's date is already a day ahead of UTC, someone added with the default join date is not yet employed by the UTC reads and changes. Fix: have these defaults use entityToday for the person's legal entity too, or record why reads may stay on UTC, and add a variant test at EVENING like add-person-today-109.
findings.scenario: At 2026-11-15T20:00Z (01:30 on the 16th in Colombo), add_person in Sri Lanka with no joinedOn gives joined_on 2026-11-16, status active. Right after, change_person with no effectiveOn uses on=2026-11-15, before the employment starts. listPeople/getPerson with on=2026-11-15 find no employment in force, so the forProject 'Add them to TMT' step that follows can't resolve the person who was just added.

findings.message: Every hour, the status job skips each entity with no time zone, and lists it only in its own audit 'after'. Before this change, those people moved by UTC. Now they don't move at all, and no screen or notification says so. Only LK has a default zone (ENTITY_ZONES), so any real AU entity without a workflows.entity_zone row is affected. Fix: surface 'unzoned' where people look, like the 'not scheduled' state with the set_entity_zone Ask button on the workflows SchedulesCard, or through a notifications rule.
findings.scenario: An AU entity has no entity_zone row, and a leaver was recorded with left_on 2026-11-20 before this change. After the 20th they stay 'active' indefinitely. The only trace is an hourly audit row with unzoned: ['…Pty Ltd'].

findings.message: monthShort is a second copy of allocations' monthLabel (months.ts:14), with a narrower parser. The service accepts YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD for through (services.ts:13), but monthShort only names YYYY-MM. A Through value of 2027-05-01 shows as typed on the button, while the start month and the done line show it as a month. Fix: accept an optional -DD in MONTH, or move one month formatter into a shared package.
findings.scenario: The model fills through='2027-05-01'. The button reads 'Add Dinesh Wickrama to TMT, Mar–2027-05-01', but done says 'Mar–May'.

findings.message: The range is named by month only, with no year. That covers ranges inside one year and misses ranges that cross a year, which the service allows (MAX_MONTHS = 24). The start month is fixed in the label as `monthLabel(month)` and Through is shown through `monthShort`, so a 13-month range shows as the same words as a one-month range. Both the confirm button (what the person approves) and `look.done` (the card's closing record of what was written) give this wrong reading. `apps/web/tests/card-month-109.test.ts` makes it the expected output ("Mar–Jan" for 2027-03..2028-01). Fix: when the end year differs from the start year, add the year to both ends ("Mar 2027–Mar 2028"), using one shared rule for the server's `range` and the client's `{through}` label. Add a test row for a range that crosses a year and one for 13 months.
findings.scenario: "add Dinesh Wickrama to TMT from 2027-03 to 2028-03" → the button reads "Add Dinesh Wickrama to TMT, Mar–Mar" and done reads "Added Dinesh Wickrama to TMT · 40% Mar–Mar", but 13 month rows (2027-03..2028-03) are written
